---
title: "Study design gallery"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.align = "center")
```

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(cohortflow)
```

One complete, copyable example per study design, from data to diagram and
table. Each uses one of the package's mock-data generators, so it runs as is;
swap in your own data and criteria.

| Design | Generator | Unit of a row | What's different |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Parallel-group RCT](#parallel-group-randomised-trial) | `mock_parallel_rct()` | participant | per-arm cascade after `randomise()` |
| [Crossover trial](#crossover-trial) | `mock_crossover()` | participant-period | sequences and periods; `count_by` |
| [Cluster RCT](#cluster-randomised-trial) | `mock_cluster_rct()` | participant | cluster rules; cluster and participant counts |
| [Stepped-wedge trial](#stepped-wedge-trial) | `mock_stepped_wedge()` | participant-period | cluster-periods; site × period grid |

## Parallel-group randomised trial

Participants are individually randomised. Losses after allocation are
reported per arm.

```{r}
dat <- mock_parallel_rct(n_participants = 400, seed = 1)

crit <- cf_criteria() |>
  include(~ !is.na(age), label = "Age recorded", category = "Age") |>
  include(~ age >= 18, label = "Aged 18 or over", category = "Age") |>
  include(~ eligible_screen, label = "Met inclusion criteria") |>
  include(~ !is.na(consent_date), label = "Consented") |>
  randomise(by = "participant_id", arms = "arm") |>
  exclude(~ withdrew, label = "Withdrew") |>
  include(~ baseline_complete, label = "Baseline complete")

flow <- apply_criteria(dat, crit, id = "participant_id")
```

```{r, fig.width = 10.2, fig.height = 6.5, fig.alt = "Parallel-group CONSORT diagram splitting into two arms after randomisation."}
as_consort_diagram(flow)
```

```{r}
as_attrition_table(flow, backend = "gt")
```

## Crossover trial

Each participant receives both treatments, in a randomised order
(sequence). The data has one row per participant per period, so rows are
identified by `event_id`, and `count_by` makes the sequence and period boxes
count participants.

```{r}
co <- mock_crossover(n_participants = 150, arm_labels = c("Drug", "Placebo"), seed = 1)

crit_co <- cf_criteria() |>
  include(~ eligible_screen, label = "Met inclusion criteria") |>
  include(~ !is.na(consent_date), label = "Consented") |>
  exclude(~ withdrew, label = "Withdrew")

flow_co <- apply_criteria(co, crit_co, id = "event_id")
```

```{r, fig.width = 6.4, fig.height = 5.4, fig.alt = "Crossover CONSORT diagram with two sequences, each showing its two treatment periods."}
as_consort_diagram(
  flow_co,
  branch_by = "sequence",
  stage_by = "period",
  stage_label_by = "arm",
  count_by = "participant_id",
  final_label = "Randomised"
)
```

The trunk counts rows (two per participant); the sequence and period boxes
count participants. To count participants throughout, apply the criteria to
one row per participant, or report participant counts from a hierarchy:

```{r}
flow_co_h <- apply_criteria(
  co, crit_co, id = "event_id",
  hierarchy = cf_hierarchy(period = "event_id", participant = "participant_id")
)
as_attrition_table(
  flow_co_h,
  levels = c("participant", "period"),
  level_labels = c("Participants", "Participant-periods"),
  backend = "gt"
)
```

## Cluster-randomised trial

Clusters (practices, schools, wards) are randomised, and participants are
recruited within them. Cluster-level rules use `group_include()` or
`group_exclude()`, and the CONSORT cluster extension asks for losses at both
levels.

```{r}
cl <- mock_cluster_rct(n_clusters = 16, n_participants = 600, seed = 7)

crit_cl <- cf_criteria() |>
  include(~ eligible_screen, label = "Met inclusion criteria") |>
  include(~ !is.na(consent_date), label = "Consented") |>
  group_include(by = "cluster_id", ~ n() >= 20,
                label = "Cluster recruited 20 or more") |>
  randomise(by = "cluster_id", arms = "arm") |>
  exclude(~ withdrew, label = "Withdrew")

flow_cl <- apply_criteria(
  cl, crit_cl, id = "participant_id",
  hierarchy = cf_hierarchy(participant = "participant_id", cluster = "cluster_id")
)
```

```{r, fig.width = 9.9, fig.height = 5.5, fig.alt = "Cluster trial CONSORT diagram at participant level, splitting into two arms after cluster randomisation."}
as_consort_diagram(flow_cl, wrap_width = 24)
```

```{r}
as_attrition_table(
  flow_cl,
  levels = c("participant", "cluster"),
  level_labels = c("Participants", "Clusters"),
  backend = "gt"
)
```

The "Consequential" column counts participants lost only because their
cluster was removed. See [Hierarchical and cluster
designs](hierarchical-designs.html#how-units-are-counted).

## Stepped-wedge trial

Every cluster starts in the control condition and crosses to the
intervention at a randomised time, so each cluster contributes to both
conditions over the periods of the trial. Results are usually reported by
period, and losses by cluster-period.

```{r}
sw <- mock_stepped_wedge(n_clusters = 8, n_participants = 400,
                         n_periods = 4, n_sites = 2, seed = 3)

crit_sw <- cf_criteria() |>
  include(~ !is.na(consent_date), label = "Consented") |>
  exclude(~ withdrew, label = "Withdrew") |>
  group_include(by = c("cluster_id", "period"), ~ n() >= 8,
                label = "Cluster-period has 8 or more")

flow_sw <- apply_criteria(
  sw, crit_sw, id = "event_id",
  hierarchy = cf_hierarchy(
    observation = "event_id",
    cluster_period = c("cluster_id", "period"),
    cluster = "cluster_id"
  )
)
```

```{r, fig.width = 8.4, fig.height = 4.4, fig.alt = "Stepped-wedge CONSORT diagram whose final box splits into the four periods."}
as_consort_diagram(flow_sw, branch_by = "period", final_label = "Analysed")
```

Attrition by site and period, with each block counted separately:

```{r}
as_attrition_table(
  flow_sw,
  backend = "gt",
  group_x = "site_id", group_x_label = "Site",
  group_y = "period", group_y_label = "Period"
)
```

And at each level of the design:

```{r}
as_attrition_table(
  flow_sw,
  levels = c("observation", "cluster_period", "cluster"),
  level_labels = c("Observations", "Cluster-periods", "Clusters"),
  backend = "gt"
)
```
